flashcards.question: Which traversal yields sorted sequence for a BST?
Worst case time complexity to search in unbalanced BST?
flashcards.answer: O(N) when the tree degenerates into a linked list

flashcards.question: Height balancing condition for an AVL tree?
flashcards.answer: Balance factor |Height(Left) - Height(Right)| <= 1 for every node

flashcards.question: Can Dijkstra's algorithm handle negative edge weights?
flashcards.answer: No! Dijkstra fails on negative weights because greedy choice cannot backtrack. Use Bellman-Ford instead.

flashcards.question: What graph property is required for Topological Sort?
flashcards.answer: The graph must be a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG).

flashcards.question: What are Coffman's four deadlock conditions?
flashcards.answer:
1. Mutual Exclusion
2. Hold & Wait
3. No Preemption
4. Circular Wait

flashcards.question: Difference between Mutex and Semaphore?
flashcards.answer: Mutex is a locking mechanism owned by 1 thread. Semaphore is a signaling mechanism (counting/binary) accessible by any thread.

flashcards.question: What causes Thrashing in virtual memory?
flashcards.answer: When the CPU spends more time swapping pages in/out of swap space than executing instructions due to excessive page faults.

modules.title: B+ Trees vs B-Trees in Disk Storage
modules.summary: Why databases use B+ Trees for range queries and sequential block reads.

flashcards.question: What is a Dirty Read anomaly?
flashcards.answer: Reading uncommitted data modified by another concurrent transaction that later rolls back.

flashcards.question: What is a Phantom Read?
flashcards.answer: A transaction re-executes a query with a range condition and finds new rows inserted by another committed transaction.

assignments.prompt: Explain AVL tree balancing and time complexity.
assignments.studentSubmission: In AVL trees, the balance factor is maintained between -1 and 1 using left and right rotations to guarantee O(log N) lookup time.

In-order traversal yielding sorted order
Time complexity: O(log N) average vs O(N) skewed worst case
Self-balancing trees (AVL / Red-Black) using tree rotations
Height balancing factor and search optimization

dsaProblems.title: Two Sum
dsaProblems.description: Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target. Use a hash map for O(n) time.

dsaProblems.title: Reverse Linked List
dsaProblems.description: Given the head of a singly linked list, reverse the list, and return the reversed list. Solve iteratively with pointers prev, curr, next in O(1) space.

dsaProblems.title: Maximum Subarray (Kadane’s Algorithm)
dsaProblems.description: Find the contiguous subarray (containing at least one number) which has the largest sum and return its sum. Maintain running sum and reset when negative.

dsaProblems.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
dsaProblems.description: Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters using variable size sliding window and hash set.

dsaProblems.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
dsaProblems.description: Given a BST, find the lowest common ancestor (LCA) node of two given nodes p and q using BST split property in O(h) time.

dsaProblems.title: Merge Intervals
dsaProblems.description: Given an array of intervals where intervals[i] = [starti, endi], merge all overlapping intervals. Sort intervals by start time first.

dsaProblems.title: Word Ladder
dsaProblems.description: Given two words, beginWord and endWord, and a dictionary wordList, return the number of words in the shortest transformation sequence. Use BFS level-by-level.

dsaProblems.title: Trapping Rain Water
dsaProblems.description: Given n non-negative integers representing an elevation map where width of each bar is 1, compute how much water it can trap after raining.
